title: Grateful Dead Live at Denver Coliseum on 1973-11-21
lineage: CD -> Cool Edit Pro v2.0 -> Samplitude Professional v9.12 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat -> CD D

ai_review.summary: Excellent soundboard recording captures a stellar November ’73 show highlighted by a flawless Playing‑in‑the‑Band sandwich, soaring Jerry solos and crisp, balanced mix.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised for its tight playing and creative setlist – the half‑step > Playing > El Paso > Playing sandwich that flows into a Dark Star jam, Wharf Rat and a plaintive Morning Dew are repeatedly called “knock‑out” moments.  Charlie Miller’s remaster delivers crystal‑clear soundboard quality with balanced guitars, keyboards and vocals, making the show a go‑to example of ‘73 Dead magic.

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly positive 5‑star reviews (20 out of 22) praise both the musical performance and the soundboard quality; only one low‑rating comment is unrelated to the show.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Charlie Miller’s remaster provides a crisp, clear mix with well‑balanced guitars, keyboards and vocals; some note slightly recessed bass due to venue acoustics but overall the sound is superb.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Creative water‑themed flow with a unique Playing sandwich that segues smoothly through El Paso, Dark Star jam and into Wharf Rat before closing on Morning Dew; pacing is praised as tight and engaging throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for melting‑face‑off guitar solos, high‑pitched flute‑like feedback during Playing jam, and a beautiful, plaintive solo on Morning Dew.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass noted as slightly low in the mix due to Coliseum acoustics but overall tight and supportive of the band’s groove.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for tasteful phasing on Wharf Rat and strong rhythm work throughout the set, especially during the Playing sandwich.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith's keyboard contributions are called out for adding depth to jams (e.g., Goin Down the Road) and complementing the improvisational flow.
